surfaceMeaning: No resolved global surface imagery; the standard grid marks unmapped terrain.
unresolved: The Maclaurin model assumes satellite-orbit alignment; a slightly triaxial fit is also compatible.
Rotation period aliases prevent an absolute surface attitude claim.
name: Gǃkúnǁʼhòmdímà
credit: Proudfoot et al. (2026), accepted PSJ; occultation and satellite-orbit constraints
shapeMeaning: Published Maclaurin model with semiaxes 329, 329, 294 km. The satellite orbit is assumed equatorial. The source also permits a slightly triaxial fit; this smooth shape is a constrained model.
orientationMeaning: J2000 pole prior RA 20.6 ± 1.5°, DEC 46.25 ± 0.32° from satellite-orbit alignment. Arbitrary meridian; 11.05 h photometric period has aliases and is not installed as a qualified sidereal spin.
introduction: A distant dwarf-planet candidate with a measured occultation silhouette. This published spheroidal model combines the occultation with its satellite’s orbit; local terrain is unresolved.
